candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

MAQABIS-OF-MOAB DIGS A PIT AND ENTERS IT UP TO HIS NECK, weeping in extreme self-mortification — one of the MOST DISTINCTIVE PENITENTIAL IMAGES in Ethiopian biblical literature. The pit-immersion-penance has no direct biblical parallel and appears unique to Meqabyan. The closest analogues are the patristic Egyptian-and-Syrian ascetic-stationary-penance practices (cf. Apophthegmata Patrum on Egyptian solitary-anchorites; Simeon Stylites's pillar-station; Theodoret of Cyrus Historia Religiosa on Syrian ascetics). The chapter as a whole is the CONVERSION CHAPTER: God responds through the prophet with a long forgiveness-speech (vv. 3-10) including a direct citation of Exodus 20:5-6 (third-and-fourth-generation / thousandth-generation formula at v. 9). Maqabis emerges from the pit (v. 11), confesses, prostrates himself at the prophet's feet, is raised.

candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

EXODUS 20:5-6 THIRD-AND-FOURTH-GENERATION / THOUSANDTH-GENERATION FORGIVENESS-FORMULA — God's response-through-the-prophet to Maqabis-of-Moab's penitence (vv. 3-10) directly quotes the Decalogue anti-idolatry epigraph: 'I am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; but showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me' (Ex 20:5-6 = Deut 5:9-10). The asymmetric ratio (3-4 generations of curse : 1000 generations of mercy = 1:250+) is the canonical formulation of THE PREPONDERANCE OF DIVINE-MERCY-OVER-WRATH that Meqabyan invokes to justify the Moabite-king's eligibility for conversion. The verse functions as the THEOLOGICAL ANCHOR for the Maqabis-of-Moab arc's possibility: even the violent-destroyer-of-Jerusalem can be received into covenant under the thousandth-generation-mercy provision. Tewahedo penitential tradition cites 2 Mq 3:9 as the canonical proof-text for unlimited-divine-mercy.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

MAQABIS-OF-MOAB EMERGES FROM THE PIT and PROSTRATES AT THE PROPHET'S FEET — the conversion-arc's structural completion (vv. 11-15). The emergence-from-pit echo: Genesis 37:24-28 + 41:14 (Joseph raised from the pit/dungeon to Pharaoh's right-hand); Jeremiah 38:6-13 (Jeremiah lifted from the cistern by Ebed-melech the Ethiopian — a textually-charged Tewahedo-favorite passage); Psalm 40:2 ('he brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay'); Psalm 88:6 (the prayer-from-the-pit). Prostration-at-the-prophet's-feet parallels: 1 Kings 18:7 (Obadiah before Elijah); 2 Kings 4:27 (the Shunammite woman before Elisha); Acts 10:25 (Cornelius before Peter — a CRUCIAL Gentile-converts-to-faith parallel). The verse marks Maqabis's RITUAL-RAISING from the death-immersion penance to standing-faith — the standard EOTC baptismal-symbolism (immersion → emergence → standing-in-the-spirit). Tewahedo conversion-rite explicitly draws on this 2 Mq 3:11 emergence-and-prostration sequence.

MAQABIS-OF-MOAB DIGS A PIT AND ENTERS IT UP TO HIS NECK, weeping in extreme self-mortification — one of the MOST DISTINCTIVE PENITENTIAL IMAGES in Ethiopian biblical literature. The pit-immersion-penance has no direct biblical parallel and appears unique to Meqabyan. The closest analogues are the patristic Egyptian-and-Syrian ascetic-stationary-penance practices (cf. Apophthegmata Patrum on Egyptian solitary-anchorites; Simeon Stylites's pillar-station; Theodoret of Cyrus Historia Religiosa on Syrian ascetics). The chapter as a whole is the CONVERSION CHAPTER: God responds through the prophet with a long forgiveness-speech (vv. 3-10) including a direct citation of Exodus 20:5-6 (third-and-fourth-generation / thousandth-generation formula at v. 9). Maqabis emerges from the pit (v. 11), confesses, prostrates himself at the prophet's feet, is raised.
